name: Pero da Covilhã reaches India + Ethiopia
summary: Portuguese spy and Arabic-speaker Pero da Covilhã, sent overland from Lisbon by João II in 1487, reaches Cairo, Aden, Calicut (Kerala), and the East African Swahili coast. Reports back to João via a Jewish go-between at Cairo; continues to Ethiopia where he reaches the Solomonic court of Eskender (Constantine II) and is held for the rest of his life as an honoured but de-facto prisoner.

_quarry.structural_significance: Provides the Portuguese crown with strategic intelligence on the Indian Ocean spice trade three years before Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape (1488) and ten years before Vasco da Gama reaches India (1498). The reports inform da Gama's choice of Calicut as his destination.
